entry.title: Henry (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the tuatara Henry (pictured), who was named after Henry VIII, was planned "to have lots of wives"?

entry.title: Hollyhock House (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Los Angeles's Hollyhock House was built for someone who lived there for only one year?

entry.title: Bonnie Blue (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a journalist attributed Bonnie Blue going viral to the "outrage economy"?

entry.title: Kerjäläisten valtakunta (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the male members of the band Dingo got bottom pats from local men during a Moroccan photoshoot for the album Kerjäläisten valtakunta?

entry.title: Inquirer News Tonight (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the editors of The Philadelphia Inquirer deliberately held back information from the newspaper's TV newscast, Inquirer News Tonight, so as not to be scooped?

entry.title: a Doctor Who story (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the villain of a Doctor Who story reappeared after 49 years?

entry.title: Leibel Bergman (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the FBI tried to convince H. Bruce Franklin that Leibel Bergman, a fellow communist activist, was an FBI informant?

entry.title: a group of K-pop fans (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a group of K-pop fans performed a dance with the goal of convincing a company to commit to 100% renewable energy?

entry.title: thumb cactus (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the thumb cactus crawls over other plants in cultivation – unless you grow it upside down?
